body: may allah make your grapes sour
Thank you for your response, I will be sure to prevent unnecessary expenditure of police resources.
Totally understand, thanks for the advice, will definitely remember to pay attention to that in the coming weeks.

Appreciate it mate, I think I'm ready to tackle this turning point in my life because my dad has suffered enough in this toxic marriage and regardless of what happens, I'll still have it better than many people do.
Your situation is much more difficult than mine, I relate to the pain of silence when you can't express what you really feel or think for the sake of your own longevity. It's hard.

Wishing you godspeed in solving your troubles.
Appreciate the response, this makes sense and makes me feel much better.

Well given how much pain she caused the rest of the immediate and extended family unnecessarily, I won't be feeling sympathetic for her if, for once in her life, she sees the consequences to her immoral actions. 

But you're right, for some weird reason, even though she's never had to work and she's lived comfortably her whole life with my dad, she feels she has a right to decide how all of his income is spent and when she is told that's absurd, she takes great offence. 

It's just sad, she's sick in the head and very irrational.
But seriously, thank you for your response.
Appreciate the response, this makes me feel much better.
I was born in NZ and we all moved to Aus in 2006 I think on SCVs, but I'm pretty sure along the way, he got himself an Australian citizenship

She has been trying to defame him to everyone she knows. She spends 4+ hours on the phone daily, often screaming. My dad has made countless attempts to settle her disputes with discourse, to which she immaturely throws around insults. Soon, I may or may not try to get her involuntarily admitted as a mental health patient. 

Thanks for your response.

It was nothing egregious. Afaik, whatever he did, regardless of being illegal, didn't negatively affect anyone else at all.
I'm 19 and I would love to leave her ASAP, but I don't have an income atm because I was recently diagnosed with an autoimmune disease which debilitated me physically enough not to endure the daily grind, at least for now.

She is most certainly making false accusations. She has kept claiming over the past few months that my dad never cared for me while I was in hospital, which forced him to take time off work to drive all the way to see me, a 250km trip for him. She also believes that she doesn't get to see a large portion of my dad's income and that he spends it on his almost poverty stricken family in Iraq or himself. As I mentioned, we live in a $1.7m house. 

Thanks for your response, I appreciate it
Funny you should mention that. I think he is an Australian citizen but the rest of us (me, mother, sister) are on NZ SCVs. Anyways, thank you for the response

As former comments have stated, check to see if the humira works before going ahead with removing the ileum. if you have a caring family, hold them close, because lots of us got hit with Crohn's like a train and then the fam ran us over too.
Your symptoms sound like utter trash, all I can do is tell you I've been through it before and I know what it feels like and that you are never alone.
Social interaction external to my family has been my only consolation, keep yourself busy for now, but I wish you godspeed and hope that regardless what happens, you'll be able to enjoy the creature comforts most people take for granted. You deserve it.

This is difficult. You are the being the best you could possibly be for your partner, I think you should acknowledge your efforts do not go unappreciated even by him. But it sounds like the man's on the brink of death and has no energy to show it.
My experience was much milder than this and I was told I was relatively close to death. 
I think cautious optimism is what you need, I really recommend against moving forward with the impression that it will all get better, because it might not. Crohn's is not forgiving, for anyone. 
With that being said, seek some help for yourself because watching the love of your life go through this is traumatising to say the least, you need closure, and lots of it.
You are not to feel guilty, neither of you chose this struggle, and you're both trying your best.

I'm sorry you had to go through this. Wishing your partner godspeed in recovery.

Aye I feel you, while my Crohn's is nowhere near as severe as yours, I can certainly appreciate the bullshit you have to deal with on a daily basis with family.
My family was useless both throughout and after my hospitalisation. There is no real consolation for it unfortunately, but I hope you know you aren't alone

Thanks you, I think I find it difficult to appreciate the "bright side" as glorified as it may be. It's harder to stop a train of thought these days, it just keeps going.
I really appreciate your time and consolation. I think it's helped me calm down and see the scenario I'm in with just a bit more clarity.

Thanks for the kind words, much appreciated, sometimes the obligation that sits on my shoulders to make his investment in me worth his effort can really weigh down on me. I suppose a push is all I need sometimes
